Convert Sequence Data to Different Formats

Source: R/frequencies.R
convert_sequence_format.Rd

convert_sequence_format() turns wide or long sequence data into one of four data frames: per-sequence state counts, per-sequence state presence (one-hot), the list of consecutive transitions, or each event paired with the one before it. It reads an event log (action set) or a wide table (one row per sequence, one column per position). The counts can serve as per-sequence behaviour profiles for the association estimators of build_network() and for build_mcml_pc(). The id columns (those that id_col names, and .rid for a wide table without id_col) are not variables and must be set aside there (id_col in build_mcml_pc(), actor in build_network()); the rid column is dropped automatically.

Usage

convert_sequence_format(
  data,
  seq_cols = NULL,
  id_col = NULL,
  action = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  format = c("frequency", "onehot", "edgelist", "follows")
)

Arguments

data

A data frame of sequences: an event log or a wide table.

seq_cols

The state columns of a wide table; setting them declares a wide table. Default NULL: every column except id_col and time. With neither action nor seq_cols, the frame must be one column or hold position columns named as a numbered run (T1, T2, ..., or 1, 2, ...), with nothing beside them but the id_col (and time) columns; anything else raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input, as does a column listed both here and in id_col or time.

id_col

The identifier column(s), copied to every output row. In an event log, each unique combination of their values is one sequence, and it is required: an event log without id_col raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input (no column is taken by position). In a wide table, each row is one sequence and no id is inferred from the data: without id_col, a row-index column .rid is added. Default NULL.

action

The column holding each event's state; setting it declares an event log. Default NULL.

time

The column that orders the events within each sequence of an event log; without it, events keep their row order. A wide table leaves it out of the state columns. Default NULL.

format

The output format: "frequency" (default), the count of each state per sequence; "onehot", whether each state occurs in the sequence (0/1); "edgelist", each pair of consecutive states (from, to); "follows", each event (act) paired with the event before it (follows).

Value

A data frame with the id column(s) first. For "frequency" and "onehot": one row per sequence, a rid column identifying the sequence, and one integer column per state, holding counts or 0/1. For "edgelist": one row per transition, with columns from and to. For "follows": one row per event after the first of its sequence, with columns act and follows. An event log's rows come out sorted by id_col.

Details

A missing state (NA or an empty string) is dropped and the states on either side are joined, so a sequence A, NA, B gives the transition A -> B. frequencies() counts no transition across a missing state instead.

See also

frequencies for building transition frequency matrices.

Examples

# Wide format input
seqs <- data.frame(V1 = c("A","B","A"), V2 = c("B","A","C"), V3 = c("A","C","B"))
convert_sequence_format(seqs, format = "frequency")
#>   .rid rid A B C
#> 1    1   1 2 1 0
#> 2    2   2 1 1 1
#> 3    3   3 1 1 1
convert_sequence_format(seqs, format = "edgelist")
#>   .rid from to
#> 1    1    A  B
#> 2    1    B  A
#> 3    2    B  A
#> 4    2    A  C
#> 5    3    A  C
#> 6    3    C  B
